coverage_gaps: Only PubMed is available; dedicated human-genetics resources such as GWAS Catalog, ClinVar, OMIM, and population-frequency databases cannot be queried directly.
Citation-graph and DOI-metadata routes are unavailable, so forward-citation completeness and citation-network expansion cannot be independently verified.
Preprint servers are unavailable, limiting coverage of unreviewed findings near the 2024-12-31 cutoff.
Trial registries, regulator databases, patent sources, and chemistry databases are unavailable; clinical-development, regulatory, prior-art, and compound-specific coverage remains out of scope.
PubMed title and abstract indexing may under-retrieve older terminology, non-English reports, substrate-negative experiments, and mechanistic details reported only in full text.
The exact-title and PMID sentinel anchors validate known records but do not establish completeness for every historical discovery account or physiological-substrate claim.
exclusion_criteria: Records mentioning LRRK2 or Parkinson disease only incidentally without genetic, enzymatic, substrate, physiological, or mechanism-relevant evidence.
Studies of non-Parkinson conditions unless they directly test a transferable LRRK2 enzymatic function, physiological substrate, or pathway needed for the brief.
Purely computational predictions without experimental validation or human genetic evidence relevant to LRRK2 variants, function, or substrates.
Therapeutic efficacy, dosing, or safety reports that provide no evidence about LRRK2 target engagement, enzymatic mechanism, substrate modulation, or disease mechanism.
Non-primary summaries used as sole support for a decision-critical genetic or mechanistic claim.
Retracted reports as affirmative evidence; retain them only to document limitations or the history of a claim.
inclusion_criteria: Publication date on or before 2024-12-31 after reconciling online-first, issue, correction, and retraction dates.
Primary human genetic studies linking LRRK2 loci or variants to Parkinson disease, parkinsonism, penetrance, pathology, or population risk.
Biochemical, structural, cellular, animal, or human-tissue studies directly testing LRRK2 enzymatic function, variant effects, substrates, phosphorylation sites, or downstream mechanisms.
Studies evaluating endogenous expression or phosphorylation, direct kinase-substrate relationships, in-vivo relevance, dose-response, rescue, genetic epistasis, or pharmacological target engagement.
Null, negative, conflicting, replication, correction, retraction, incomplete-penetrance, and heterogeneous-neuropathology evidence relevant to claim strength or generalizability.
Reviews or meta-analyses used for terminology expansion, historical context, or citation leads, with substantive mechanistic conclusions traced to primary records.
Records in any language when the available English title or abstract supports eligibility assessment and the full evidence can be interpreted reliably.

queries.purpose: Recover the two 2004 PARK8/LRRK2 genetic-discovery anchor records and verify target and disease terminology.
Recover the anchor study nominating Rab proteins as LRRK2 substrates and validate substrate terminology.
queries.query: "Phosphoproteomics reveals that Parkinson's disease kinase LRRK2 regulates a subset of Rab GTPases"[Title]

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: from database inception through 2024-12-31, identify human genetic discovery and disease-associated LRRK2 variants in Parkinson disease, determine how variant effects on kinase and ROC-COR GTPase functions connect to physiological substrates and cellular pathology, and assess human, animal, cellular, biochemical, neuropathological, null, and conflicting evidence that constrains causality, penetrance, substrate status, or generalizability. Include all languages when an English title or abstract permits screening; use reviews for terminology and citation leads while grounding mechanistic claims in primary studies.
stop_rules: Execute all twelve planned PubMed query events and preserve each exact query, execution timestamp, requested cutoff, result count, and provider version when available.
Do not begin broad screening until Q01 recovers both genetic-discovery anchors and Q02 recovers the Rab-substrate anchor; revise terminology within the fixed query budget if an anchor is missed.
Deduplicate canonical records by PMID and DOI while preserving every query-to-record occurrence and wave assignment.
Complete screening for genetic discovery, high-penetrance and risk variants, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrates, downstream biology, and limiting evidence before synthesis.
Stop expansion after two consecutive independently screened expansion passes add no new decision-relevant variant, substrate, mechanism, or counterevidence category.
Stop at the twelve-event query cap and report any unfinished branch or missed anchor as a coverage gap rather than silently extending the search.
Apply the 2024-12-31 publication cutoff after retrieval when PubMed indexing or date syntax is ambiguous, and document records excluded during date reconciliation.
Escalate conflicting duplicate metadata, disputed direct-substrate status, or irreconcilable variant-effect results for manual adjudication; do not collapse them into a single conclusion.

End retrieval when the planned route is complete, anchors are recovered, every decision-critical claim has supporting and challenge evidence or an explicit gap, and further PubMed searching is unlikely to change the mechanistic assessment.
